data.gender_notes: Alban is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'Albus', meaning 'white' or 'noble'. Alban is a name of ancient Roman origin, commonly given to boys in Christianity as a nod to Saint Alban, the first British martyr. The name Alban carries the meaning “Noble or Handsome” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Alban usually hope their child will grow to embody noble or handsome and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes purity and nobility in faith.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alban total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Alban, a noble Roman, converted to Christianity and shielded a Christian priest from persecution during the Roman Empire. When the priest's identity was discovered, it was Alban who took the place of the priest and was sentenced to death, thus becoming the first recorded British martyr and an important figure in English history. The name Alban is deeply rooted in British and Christian heritage, symbolizing courage, loyalty, and sacrifice.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Alban holds spiritual significance as it is the namesake of the first known British martyr and a symbol of the early Christian community's steadfastness and devotion. The name is also a reminder of one's personal commitment to their beliefs, as Alban willingly sacrificed his life to protect another's faith. The name Alban invokes the virtues of compassion, forgiveness, devotion, and belief, encouraging individuals to embody these qualities in their daily lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Alban, meaning "noble" or "handsome," represents the inner beauty and nobility of faith in God. Like the early Christian martyr St. Alban, who gave up his worldly possessions and protected a priest during persecution, the name inspires one to embody selflessness and courage in the face of adversity.
